idea: A bumblebee: a fat, furry worker, warm yellow and black, dusted with pollen, a white tail.
world: A garden in June. A bumblebee is a heavy, round, gentle thing in a thick coat of fur, built to be warm in the cold and to carry pollen home; nothing about it is sharp. Its colours are a warning worn softly: broad bands of velvet black and ochre yellow, a white tip to its tail. Its legs and eyes are the only hard, shiny parts. It comes home yellow with dust.

signature.says: The bands. Broad bands of black and yellow run across the car, round its whole body, the way they ring a bee's abdomen: wide, few, and furred. No band has a hard edge: where two colours meet, their hairs cross into each other over a centimetre or two. The last band at the tail is white. A band's edge sits on or beside one of the car's own crosswise lines where there is one, and simply crosses the surface where there isn't: fur doesn't follow panels. The inner car and the wheels are the bee's black legs: hard and shiny, the only shine on the car.

dna.says: Everything on the body is fur. A colour's edge is a fringe of hairs 1 to 2 cm long lying with the car's flow, nose to tail, crossing into the next colour; up close, a band is thousands of hairs, and their nap catches the light differently where the body bends. Shapes are fat and rounded, never pointed, never outlined. Pollen is a dust of pale grains that gathers where dust would: in hollows, at a lip, along a crease's foot, thicker low down. Sizes: a band 40 to 80 cm, a hair 1 to 2 cm, a grain of pollen 1 to 2 mm. Rhythm: wide, wider, narrow, white.

colours.name: Bee yellow
colours.job: leads: the yellow bands, warm ochre, never lemon

colours.name: Velvet black
colours.job: the black bands, a brown-black with depth, and the legs

colours.name: Tail white
colours.job: the last band at the tail, a warm cream white

colours.name: Pollen
colours.job: the dust: pale grains in the hollows and low down

colours.name: Wing amber
colours.job: the glass: a smoky amber tint, the wings' veins

meet: Colours never meet on a line: they meet in fur, each one's hairs reaching into the other. Pollen lies on any colour, as dust. Amber appears only in the glass.

surfaces.job: the yellow fur: a nap with no shine at all
the black fur, the same nap
the legs and the eyes: the inner car and the wheels, hard black chitin
the tyres: the feet, matte black
the wings: the glass, smoky amber, the only clear shine

ageing: A worker a few weeks into summer: the fur is thick and even, flattened a little where it brushes the flowers (the top's front, the flanks' widest point), and pollen has caught in it, most where it's hard to clean. No wear, no dirt, no scratches: a bee is never damaged, only dusty.

large.what: four bands round the whole body: black, yellow, black, white tail, wide and few
